goal: Correct comment wording in src/delivery/create-customer-asgi-composition.mjs that could be read as claiming Uvicorn/Hypercorn can call our JavaScript ASGI-shaped callable directly. Uvicorn and Hypercorn are Python ASGI servers; this package's callable is ASGI-protocol-shaped and host-adapter-ready at the boundary, but direct Uvicorn/Hypercorn hosting requires a separate Python host bridge/shim that this package does not implement. No behavior change; no host selected.

kernelReady, sdkReady, appBuildable, releaseAllowed, deployAllowed, productionAllowed, runnableProduct all stay false

scopeResolution.note: src/delivery/create-customer-asgi-composition.mjs previously described the returned app callable as 'a function a host adapter (Uvicorn, Hypercorn, ...) can call directly', which reads as if a Python ASGI server can invoke our JavaScript function in-process. That is not true: Uvicorn and Hypercorn are Python processes that call Python ASGI callables; our `app` is a JavaScript async (scope, receive, send) function that is ASGI-protocol-shaped (its call signature and event vocabulary match the ASGI spec) and is host-adapter-ready at that protocol boundary, but wiring it to a real Uvicorn or Hypercorn process needs a separate Python host bridge/shim outside this package -- not implemented here. This package corrects the module docblock, the createCustomerAsgiComposition JSDoc, and the two encoder helper comments (encodeJsonBody, encodeUtf8HeaderPart) to state that boundary precisely, without touching any executable statement, export, or control-flow line.

red.note: Before this fix, the source file still contained the wording 'a host adapter (Uvicorn, Hypercorn, ...) can call directly' immediately after describing `app` as a plain JavaScript async function, with no mention anywhere in the file of a required separate Python host bridge/shim. The new test's assertions that this old wording is gone and that the new boundary-truth wording (ASGI-shaped, host-adapter-ready at the protocol boundary, direct Uvicorn/Hypercorn hosting needs a separate Python host bridge/shim not implemented here) is present both failed against that prior wording.
